::: {.callout-note}
## Source inspected
The public history page was read on 20 September 2026. It is a later organizational timeline, not a contemporaneous 1980s record.
:::

## Annotation

The page states that the BC Division of the Canadian Paraplegic Association began in 1957; that Doug Mowat “accepts the role of Executive Director” in 1960; and that in 1985 “Creekview opens near Granville Island in Vancouver. Creekview was the world’s first integrated, self-managed housing project with shared support services for people with high-level quadriplegia.”

It does not mention CSIL, ECPM, *Keys on Freedom*, or a 1987 evaluation. The 1985 Creekview sentence is a later institutional claim. It is catalogued here because it is a public, inspectable statement — not because this archive has verified “world’s first.”

## Open questions

- Sources SCI BC used for the 1985 Creekview sentence.
- Why a later SCI BC article about Walt Lawrence says “Creekside” rather than “Creekview.”
